title: Cost minimization with isoquants and isocosts
summary: The rule MPL/w = MPK/r, the tangency picture, what happens when the wage falls, and the session's conclusion.

chunks.heading: The cost-minimizing rule
chunks.explanation_md:
To produce a given output at the lowest cost, the **marginal product per dollar spent should be equal for all inputs**:

**MPL / w = MPK / r**

Rearranged, that is **MPL / MPK = w / r**, and since MPL/MPK is the MRTS, the rule is simply **MRTS_KL = w / r**.

Why: if a dollar spent on labour bought more output than a dollar on capital, the firm could shift spending towards labour and make the same output for less.
chunks.exam_line: Cost is minimised where MPL/w = MPK/r, which is MRTS_KL = w/r.

check_questions.stem: At the cost-minimising input mix, the marginal product per dollar spent is equal for all inputs.

chunks.heading: The picture: where the isoquant touches the isocost
chunks.explanation_md:
Draw K on the vertical axis and L on the horizontal. The **isoquant** Q shows the output needed; the **isocost** lines show cost levels.

The **point of cost minimization** is where the isoquant just **touches** (is tangent to) the **lowest isocost line** it can reach. At that point the **slope of the isocost equals the slope of the isoquant**, which is the same as MRTS_KL = w/r.
chunks.exam_line: Cost minimization: the isoquant is tangent to the lowest isocost; slope of isocost = slope of isoquant. (Draw the diagram.)

check_questions.answer: Tangent to the lowest isocost line it can reach

check_questions.stem: At the cost-minimizing point, the slope of the isocost equals the slope of the isoquant.

chunks.heading: When the wage falls: optimal input substitution
chunks.explanation_md:
The firm makes Q0 at point A, using L0 and K0, at cost C0.

Now the wage falls from **w0 to w1**. The isocost line **rotates counterclockwise**, because labour is now cheaper relative to capital.

To make the same Q0, the firm moves to **point B** on a **lower isocost line C1**: it uses **more labour (L0 to L1)** and **less capital (K0 to K1)**. It substitutes towards the input that became cheaper.
chunks.exam_line: A lower wage rotates the isocost; to make the same output the firm moves along the isoquant to more labour, less capital, at a lower cost.

check_questions.stem: If the wage falls, to make the same output Q0 the firm uses:
options: The same mix at a higher cost

check_questions.stem: When the wage falls, the isocost line rotates counterclockwise.

chunks.heading: The session's conclusion
chunks.explanation_md:
- To maximise profit (or minimise cost), managers use inputs so that the value of the marginal product of each input reflects the price the firm pays for it.
- The **optimal mix of inputs** is reached when **MRTS_KL = w/r**.
- **Cost functions** are the foundation for working out profit-maximising behaviour.

check_questions.stem: The optimal mix of inputs is achieved when MRTS_KL = w/r.

questions.stem: MPL/MPK = w/r is the same condition as:
After a fall in the wage, the firm's new cost-minimising point B for the same output lies on:
Utilizing the isoquant and isocost curves, explain the cost minimization principle.
questions.model_answer_md:
A firm wants to make a given output at the **lowest cost**.

- **Isoquant:** the combinations of K and L that give the same output. Its slope is the MRTS_KL = MPL/MPK.
- **Isocost:** the combinations that cost the same, wL + rK = C, with slope w/r.
- **Rule:** marginal product per dollar must be equal for all inputs, **MPL/w = MPK/r**, which is **MRTS_KL = w/r**.
- **Diagram:** the cost-minimising point is where the isoquant is **tangent to the lowest isocost line** it can reach, so the slope of the isocost equals the slope of the isoquant. (Draw K on the vertical axis, L on the horizontal, the isoquant and three isocosts, and mark the tangency.)

If the wage falls, the isocost rotates and the firm moves along the isoquant to more labour and less capital at a lower cost.
